subproblems.title: A linear subspace is determined by its intersection with a ball centred at one of its points
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q₁, Q₂ be linear subspaces of ℝ^P, let x ∈ Q₁ and t > 0. If Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x) (open balls), then Q₁ = Q₂.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q₁ Q₂ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (t : ℝ), x ∈ Q₁ → 0 < t → (Q₁ : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x t = (Q₂ : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x t → Q₁ = Q₂
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (b) of the parent proof of idtp_tdc_density_locally_constant.
1. dist x x = 0 < t, so x ∈ Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x); hence x ∈ Q₂.
2. Claim. Let Q, Q' be subspaces with x ∈ Q, x ∈ Q' and Q ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q'. Then Q ≤ Q'. Proof: let v ∈ Q and put s := t / (2(‖v‖ + 1)) > 0. Then x + s • v ∈ Q, as Q is a subspace containing x and v. Also dist (x + s • v) x = ‖s • v‖ = s‖v‖ = t‖v‖/(2(‖v‖ + 1)) < t. So x + s • v ∈ Q ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q'. As x ∈ Q', s • v = (x + s • v) − x ∈ Q', and v = s⁻¹ • (s • v) ∈ Q' since s ≠ 0.
3. Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q₂, so step 2 with (Q, Q') := (Q₁, Q₂) gives Q₁ ≤ Q₂. Q₂ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q₁, so step 2 with (Q, Q') := (Q₂, Q₁) gives Q₂ ≤ Q₁ (x ∈ Q₂ by step 1). By antisymmetry, Q₁ = Q₂. ∎
proof_key_steps: x ∈ Q₂, because x ∈ Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x).
If x ∈ Q ∩ Q' and Q ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q', then for v ∈ Q the point x + s•v with s = t/(2(‖v‖+1)) lies in Q ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q'. So s•v ∈ Q' and v ∈ Q'; hence Q ≤ Q'.
Apply this in both directions and conclude by antisymmetry.

subproblems.title: Radial projection to the unit sphere at most doubles the distance to a unit vector
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and y, w ∈ ℝ^P with y ≠ 0 and |w| = 1. Then |y/|y| − w| ≤ 2|y − w|.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (e) of the parent proof of idtp_tdc_density_locally_constant.
1. ‖y‖ > 0, as y ≠ 0. ‖y‖⁻¹ • y − y = (‖y‖⁻¹ − 1) • y, so ‖‖y‖⁻¹ • y − y‖ = |‖y‖⁻¹ − 1| · ‖y‖ = |1 − ‖y‖|.
2. As ‖w‖ = 1, |1 − ‖y‖| = |‖w‖ − ‖y‖| ≤ ‖w − y‖ = ‖y − w‖ (reverse triangle inequality abs_norm_sub_norm_le).
3. By the triangle inequality and steps 1–2, ‖‖y‖⁻¹ • y − w‖ ≤ ‖‖y‖⁻¹ • y − y‖ + ‖y − w‖ ≤ 2‖y − w‖. ∎
proof_key_steps: |1 − ‖y‖| = |‖w‖ − ‖y‖| ≤ ‖y − w‖ by the reverse triangle inequality.
By the triangle inequality, ‖‖y‖⁻¹•y − w‖ ≤ ‖‖y‖⁻¹•y − y‖ + ‖y − w‖ ≤ 2‖y − w‖.

subproblems.title: An upper semicontinuous, dilation-invariant density function of a 2-dimensional minimizing cone, a positive integer on its support away from the vertex
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟₂(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and a cone (IsConeCurrent C). Suppose spt C contains some p ≠ 0. Then there is Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with the following properties: HasMassDensity C y Θ(y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P; Θ is upper semicontinuous; for every q ∈ spt C with q ≠ 0 there is m ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1 and Θ(q) = m; and Θ(s·x) = Θ(x) for all s > 0 and x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2), IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → (∃ p ∈ C.support, p ≠ 0) → ∃ Θ : Euclid P → ℝ, (∀ y : Euclid P, HasMassDensity C y (Θ y)) ∧ UpperSemicontinuous Θ ∧ (∀ q ∈ C.support, q ≠ 0 → ∃ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m ∧ Θ q = (m : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ (s : ℝ) (x : Euclid P), 0 < s → Θ (s • x) = Θ x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 and facts (a), (c) of the parent proof of idtp_tdc_density_locally_constant, packaged with the hypothesis 'some p ∈ spt C has p ≠ 0' in place of the parent's point p₀.
0. Facts.
   - (a) Uniqueness of densities: for every y and θ, θ' ∈ ℝ, HasMassDensity C y θ and HasMassDensity C y θ' imply θ = θ'. This is exactly the accepted cross-branch declaration Submission.dimred_cs_mi_hasMassDensity_unique (applied to P, 2, univ, C, y, θ, θ').
   - Direct proof of (a): both hypotheses give 0 ≤ θ and 0 ≤ θ', and limits ENNReal.ofReal θ and ENNReal.ofReal θ' of the same function along 𝓝[>] 0, which is a nontrivial filter. [0, ∞] is Hausdorff, so the limits agree (tendsto_nhds_unique). ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff (for nonnegative arguments) then gives θ = θ'.
   - (c) C is integer multiplicity, being the first component of IsMinimizingIn C univ. So for every s > 0 the sibling Submission.idtp_tdc_cone_dilation (P, 2, C) gives HasMassDensity C (s • x) θ ↔ HasMassDensity C x θ for all x and θ.
1. (P ≥ 2.) Let p ∈ spt C with p ≠ 0. Put lams j := 1/(j + 1). Then lams j > 0 and lams → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat). Apply the parent's prerequisite Submission.idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar to P, C, its three hypotheses, p, these lams and this limit. Among other data it yields an orthonormal family τ : Fin 2 → ℝ^P. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so 2 = card (Fin 2) ≤ finrank ℝ (Euclid P) = P (LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
2. (Monotonicity.) Apply the cross-branch theorem Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity with P, n := 2, d := P, U := univ, N := univ and T := C. Its hypotheses hold as follows.
   - 1 ≤ 2 holds. 2 ≤ P holds by step 1, and P ≤ P is trivial. univ is open.
   - IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 P univ holds. For every y take V := univ ⊆ Euclid P, W := univ and ψ := id : Euclid P → Euclid P. Then V and W are open and y ∈ W. id is C² on univ (contDiff_id.contDiffOn) and injective, and id '' univ = univ = univ ∩ univ. For compact K, univ ∩ id ⁻¹' K = K is compact. fderiv ℝ id z = ContinuousLinearMap.id (fderiv_id), which is injective.
   - (closure univ \ univ) ∩ univ = ∅, because closure univ \ univ = ∅.
   - IsMinimizingIn C (univ ∩ univ) is IsMinimizingIn C univ after rewriting univ ∩ univ = univ (Set.inter_self).
   - C.support ⊆ univ ∩ univ holds trivially, and BoundaryVanishes C is a hypothesis.
   The third conjunct of the conclusion supplies Θ : Euclid P → ℝ with HasMassDensity C y (Θ y) for every y ∈ univ, i.e. for every y. It also gives UpperSemicontinuousOn Θ univ, which is UpperSemicontinuous Θ by upperSemicontinuousOn_univ_iff. These are the first two claims.
3. (Positive integer values.) Let q ∈ spt C with q ≠ 0. Submission.idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar applied at q (with the same lams) gives c ∈ ℤ with 1 ≤ c.natAbs and HasMassDensity C q (c.natAbs : ℝ). Step 2 gives HasMassDensity C q (Θ q), so (a) gives Θ q = c.natAbs. Take m := c.natAbs; then 1 ≤ m and Θ q = (m : ℝ).
4. (Dilation invariance.) Let s > 0 and x ∈ ℝ^P. Step 2 gives HasMassDensity C x (Θ x), so (c) gives HasMassDensity C (s • x) (Θ x). Step 2 also gives HasMassDensity C (s • x) (Θ (s • x)), so (a) gives Θ (s • x) = Θ x.
5. Hence Θ has all four properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar at p gives an orthonormal τ : Fin 2 → ℝ^P, so P ≥ 2.
dimred_minimizing_monotonicity with n = 2, d = P, U = N = univ (identity chart) gives Θ with HasMassDensity C y (Θ y) for every y and Θ upper semicontinuous.
At q ∈ spt C ∖ {0}, idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar gives HasMassDensity C q |c| with |c| ≥ 1. By uniqueness of densities (dimred_cs_mi_hasMassDensity_unique), Θ q = |c|.
idtp_tdc_cone_dilation and uniqueness of densities give Θ(s•x) = Θ(x) for s > 0.

subproblems.title: A point of locally constant density whose nearby equal-density sphere points are stable carries a planar disc of uniform radius
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟₂(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P, with ∂C = 0 and a cone. Let z ∈ spt C with |z| = 1, let k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, and let δ > 0 be such that HasMassDensity C y k for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(z). Let L > 0, and assume (H): every a ∈ spt C with |a| = 1, a ∈ B_L(z) and HasMassDensity C a k admits δ' > 0 and k' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C y k' for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ'(a). Then there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with dim Q = 2 and z ∈ Q with the following property. Put ρ := min(1/2, L/4). Every x ∈ Q ∩ B_ρ(z) admits ε > 0 such that spt C ∩ B_ε(x) = Q ∩ B_ε(x), HasMassDensity C y k for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(x), and H²(W ∩ Q) ≤ M_W(C) for every open W ⊆ B_ε(x). Here H² = μHE[2] and M_W = massOn.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7–10 and facts (b), (c), (e) of the parent proof of idtp_tdc_density_locally_constant, for one light point.
- The parent's z_i, k_i, δ_i and arc half-length r'/2 become z, k, δ and L.
- The parent's derivation of the endpoint hypothesis from 'a ∉ J' is replaced by hypothesis (H) below.
- The disc radius ρ := min(1/2, L/4) is the parent's ρ₀ = min(1/2, r'/8) with L = r'/2.
Hypotheses: C minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂C = 0, C a cone; z ∈ spt C, ‖z‖ = 1; k ≥ 1; δ > 0 with HasMassDensity C y k for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(z); L > 0.
(H): every a ∈ spt C with ‖a‖ = 1, a ∈ B_L(z) and HasMassDensity C a k has δ' > 0 and k' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C y k' for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ'(a).
0. Facts.
   - (b) The sibling Submission.idtp_tdc_dlc_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball_eq: x ∈ Q₁, t > 0 and Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x) imply Q₁ = Q₂.
   - (e) The sibling Submission.idtp_tdc_dlc_normalize_dist_le: y ≠ 0 and ‖w‖ = 1 imply ‖‖y‖⁻¹ • y − w‖ ≤ 2‖y − w‖.
   - (c) C is integer multiplicity (first component of IsMinimizingIn C univ). For s > 0, Submission.idtp_tdc_cone_dilation (P, 2, C, s) gives s • x ∈ spt C ↔ x ∈ spt C and HasMassDensity C (s • x) θ ↔ HasMassDensity C x θ, for all x and θ.
   - Good. For the subspace Q fixed in step 1 and w ∈ ℝ^P, Good(w) means: ∃ ε > 0 with spt C ∩ B_ε(w) = Q ∩ B_ε(w) and HasMassDensity C y k for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(w).
   - Restriction. If Good(w) holds with ε, it holds with every t ∈ (0, ε]. Intersect both sides of the set equation with B_t(w) ⊆ B_ε(w).
1. (The plane at z.) z ≠ 0, since ‖z‖ = 1. Apply the parent's prerequisite Submission.idtp_cone_constant_density_planar to P, C, p := z, k and δ. Its hypotheses are the three hypotheses on C, z ∈ spt C, z ≠ 0, 0 < δ and the density hypothesis. It gives δ₁ > 0 and a subspace Q with finrank ℝ Q = 2, z ∈ Q and spt C ∩ B_δ₁(z) = Q ∩ B_δ₁(z). Fix this Q; it is the subspace of the conclusion.
2. (An orthonormal basis (z, e) of Q.)
   - The line ℝ∙z has finrank 1 (finrank_span_singleton, z ≠ 0), and finrank Q = 2. If Q ≤ ℝ∙z then 2 ≤ 1 (Submodule.finrank_mono), which is false. So some u ∈ Q has u ∉ ℝ∙z.
   - Put v := u − ⟨z, u⟩ z ∈ Q. Then v ≠ 0, since otherwise u = ⟨z, u⟩ z ∈ ℝ∙z. Also ⟨z, v⟩ = ⟨z, u⟩ − ⟨z, u⟩‖z‖² = 0.
   - Put e := ‖v‖⁻¹ • v ∈ Q. Then ‖e‖ = 1 and ⟨z, e⟩ = 0. The same holds for −e ∈ Q.
   - (z, e) is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, and span{z, e} ≤ Q. Both have finrank 2, so span{z, e} = Q (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).
   - Consequently every w ∈ Q satisfies w = ⟨w, z⟩ z + ⟨w, e⟩ e. Indeed d := w − ⟨w, z⟩ z − ⟨w, e⟩ e lies in Q = span{z, e} and has ⟨d, z⟩ = ⟨d, e⟩ = 0. Writing d = αz + βe gives ‖d‖² = α⟨d, z⟩ + β⟨d, e⟩ = 0, so d = 0.
3. (Arcs.) Let ϵ ∈ {e, −e}. Apply the sibling Submission.idtp_tdc_arc_continuation to P, C, Q, z, ϵ, k and L. Its hypotheses hold as follows.
   - The three hypotheses on C hold; finrank Q = 2; z ∈ Q; ϵ ∈ Q; ‖z‖ = 1; ‖ϵ‖ = 1; inner ℝ z ϵ = 0; 1 ≤ k.
   - (i) ε₀ := min(δ, δ₁) > 0 works. By restriction of step 1, spt C ∩ B_ε₀(z) = Q ∩ B_ε₀(z). Every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε₀(z) ⊆ B_δ(z) has HasMassDensity C y k.
   - (ii) Let 0 < φ < L and a := cos φ • z + sin φ • ϵ, with a ∈ spt C and HasMassDensity C a k. As z ⊥ ϵ are unit vectors, ‖a‖² = cos²φ + sin²φ = 1 and ‖a − z‖² = (cos φ − 1)² + sin²φ = 2 − 2 cos φ. Since 1 − φ²/2 ≤ cos φ (Real.one_sub_sq_div_two_le_cos), ‖a − z‖² ≤ φ². So ‖a − z‖ ≤ φ < L, i.e. a ∈ B_L(z). (H) now gives δ' > 0 and k' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C y k' for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ'(a), which is (ii).
   The sibling yields Good(cos φ • z + sin φ • ϵ) for every φ with 0 ≤ φ < L, for both ϵ = e and ϵ = −e.
4. (Unit vectors of Q near z are Good.) Let w ∈ Q with ‖w‖ = 1 and ‖w − z‖ < L/2.
   - Put α := ⟨w, z⟩ and β := ⟨w, e⟩. Then w = α z + β e by step 2, and α² + β² = ‖w‖² = 1, so −1 ≤ α ≤ 1.
   - Let θ := arccos α ∈ [0, π] (Real.arccos_nonneg, Real.arccos_le_pi). Then cos θ = α (Real.cos_arccos), and sin θ = √(1 − α²) = √(β²) = |β| (Real.sin_arccos, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
   - Let ϵ := e if β ≥ 0 and ϵ := −e if β < 0. In both cases sin θ • ϵ = β e, so w = cos θ • z + sin θ • ϵ.
   - ‖w − z‖² = ‖w‖² − 2⟨w, z⟩ + ‖z‖² = 2 − 2α = 2 − 2 cos θ = 4 sin²(θ/2), using cos θ = cos(2·(θ/2)) = 1 − 2 sin²(θ/2) (Real.cos_two_mul_eq_one_sub).
   - Since θ/2 ∈ [0, π/2], Jordan's inequality (Real.mul_le_sin) gives sin(θ/2) ≥ (2/π)(θ/2) = θ/π ≥ 0. Hence ‖w − z‖ = 2 sin(θ/2) ≥ 2θ/π.
   - Therefore θ ≤ (π/2)‖w − z‖ < (π/2)(L/2) = πL/4 ≤ L (Real.pi_le_four). Since 0 ≤ θ < L, step 3 for this ϵ gives Good(w).
   This is the parent's angle parametrization of step 9, φ := arg(α + iβ), written as |φ| = θ with the sign absorbed into ϵ = ±e.
5. (Every point of the disc is Good.) Put ρ := min(1/2, L/4) and let x ∈ Q ∩ B_ρ(z).
   - ‖x‖ ≥ ‖z‖ − ‖x − z‖ > 1 − 1/2 = 1/2, so x ≠ 0. Put s := ‖x‖ > 0 and w := s⁻¹ • x ∈ Q. Then ‖w‖ = 1.
   - By (e) with y := x and w := z, ‖w − z‖ ≤ 2‖x − z‖ < 2ρ ≤ L/2. So step 4 gives Good(w) with some ε > 0.
   - We claim Good(x) holds with s·ε > 0. For y ∈ ℝ^P we have ‖s⁻¹ • y − w‖ = s⁻¹‖y − x‖, so y ∈ B_{sε}(x) ⟺ s⁻¹ • y ∈ B_ε(w). Also y ∈ spt C ⟺ s⁻¹ • y ∈ spt C, by (c) with factor s⁻¹. And y ∈ Q ⟺ s⁻¹ • y ∈ Q, as Q is a subspace and s ≠ 0.
   - Hence y ∈ spt C ∩ B_{sε}(x) ⟺ s⁻¹ • y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(w) = Q ∩ B_ε(w) ⟺ y ∈ Q ∩ B_{sε}(x).
   - For y ∈ spt C ∩ B_{sε}(x), Good(w) gives HasMassDensity C (s⁻¹ • y) k. Then (c) with factor s and point s⁻¹ • y gives HasMassDensity C (s • (s⁻¹ • y)) k, i.e. HasMassDensity C y k.
6. (Mass bound.) Let x ∈ Q ∩ B_ρ(z), and let ε_x > 0 witness Good(x) (step 5).
   - x ∈ Q ∩ B_{ε_x}(x) = spt C ∩ B_{ε_x}(x), so x ∈ spt C; and x ≠ 0.
   - Apply Submission.idtp_cone_constant_density_planar to P, C, p := x, k and δ := ε_x, with the density hypothesis taken from Good(x). It gives δ₂ > 0 and a subspace Q₂ with spt C ∩ B_δ₂(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_δ₂(x) and C.massOn W = (k : ℝ≥0∞) · μHE[2](W ∩ Q₂) for every open W ⊆ B_δ₂(x).
   - Put t := min(ε_x, δ₂) > 0. By restriction, Q ∩ B_t(x) = spt C ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x). Since x ∈ Q, (b) gives Q = Q₂.
   - Then ε := t has all three required properties. spt C ∩ B_t(x) = Q ∩ B_t(x) and HasMassDensity C y k for y ∈ spt C ∩ B_t(x), by restriction of Good(x). For open W ⊆ B_t(x) ⊆ B_δ₂(x), μHE[2](W ∩ Q) = 1 · μHE[2](W ∩ Q) ≤ (k : ℝ≥0∞) · μHE[2](W ∩ Q) = C.massOn W, because 1 ≤ k.
7. Q satisfies finrank ℝ Q = 2 and z ∈ Q (step 1), and step 6 gives the required ε for every x ∈ Q ∩ B_{min(1/2, L/4)}(z). ∎
proof_key_steps: idtp_cone_constant_density_planar at z gives a plane Q ∋ z with spt C ∩ B_δ₁(z) = Q ∩ B_δ₁(z).
Gram–Schmidt gives a unit e ∈ Q with e ⊥ z. Then Q = span{z, e} and w = ⟨w,z⟩z + ⟨w,e⟩e for w ∈ Q.
idtp_tdc_arc_continuation along ϵ = ±e for angles in [0, L) makes every arc point Good. Its endpoint hypothesis follows from (H), since arc points are unit vectors with ‖a − z‖ ≤ φ < L.
A unit vector w ∈ Q with ‖w − z‖ < L/2 equals cos θ z + sin θ (±e) with θ = arccos⟨w,z⟩ ≤ (π/2)‖w − z‖ < L (Jordan's inequality and π ≤ 4), so w is Good.
Cone dilation (idtp_tdc_cone_dilation) and normalize_dist_le make every x ∈ Q ∩ B_{min(1/2, L/4)}(z) Good, with radius ‖x‖ε.
idtp_cone_constant_density_planar at x plus subspace_eq_of_inter_ball_eq give C.massOn W = k·H²(W ∩ Q) ≥ H²(W ∩ Q) for open W near x.

subproblems.title: Planar discs of uniform radius accumulating at an unstable point contradict finite mass
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let C ∈ 𝒟₂(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity, and let ρ > 0. For i ∈ ℕ let Q_i be linear subspaces of ℝ^P with dim Q_i = 2, z_i ∈ Q_i with z_i → b ∈ ℝ^P, and k_i ∈ ℕ. Assume every x ∈ Q_i ∩ B_ρ(z_i) admits ε > 0 such that spt C ∩ B_ε(x) = Q_i ∩ B_ε(x), HasMassDensity C y k_i for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(x), and H²(W ∩ Q_i) ≤ M_W(C) for every open W ⊆ B_ε(x). Assume also that b is unstable: there are no ε > 0 and m ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C y m for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(b). Then these hypotheses are contradictory (False).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (Q : ℕ → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (z : ℕ → Euclid P) (k : ℕ → ℕ) (b : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), IsIntegerMultiplicity C → 0 < ρ → (∀ i, Module.finrank ℝ (Q i) = 2) → (∀ i, z i ∈ Q i) → Tendsto z atTop (𝓝 b) → (∀ i, ∀ x ∈ (Q i : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball (z i) ρ, ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ C.support ∩ ball x ε = (Q i : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x ε ∧ (∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball x ε → HasMassDensity C y (k i)) ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ ball x ε → μHE[2] (W ∩ (Q i : Set (Euclid P))) ≤ C.massOn W) → (¬ ∃ (ε : ℝ) (m : ℕ), 0 < ε ∧ ∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball b ε → HasMassDensity C y m) → False
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 11–14 of the parent proof of idtp_tdc_density_locally_constant. The parent's light-point planes, centres, densities, accumulation point and uniform disc radius become the arbitrary data Q, z, k, b, ρ, and 'b ∈ J' is replaced by the instability hypothesis on b.
0. Notation and facts. D_i := Q_i ∩ B_ρ(z_i). For x ∈ D_i, the hypothesis supplies ε > 0 with three properties: (G1) spt C ∩ B_ε(x) = Q_i ∩ B_ε(x); (G2) HasMassDensity C y (k i) for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(x); (G3) μHE[2](W ∩ Q_i) ≤ C.massOn W for every open W ⊆ B_ε(x).
   - Restriction: if (G1) holds with ε and 0 < t ≤ ε, then spt C ∩ B_t(x) = Q_i ∩ B_t(x). Intersect both sides of (G1) with B_t(x) ⊆ B_ε(x).
   - (b) Uniqueness of planes is the sibling Submission.idtp_tdc_dlc_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball_eq: if x ∈ Q₁, t > 0 and Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x), then Q₁ = Q₂.
1. (Discs on distinct planes are disjoint.) Let i, j satisfy Q i ≠ Q j, and suppose x ∈ D_i ∩ D_j. The hypothesis gives ε₁ > 0 for (i, x) and ε₂ > 0 for (j, x). Put t := min(ε₁, ε₂) > 0. By restriction, Q_i ∩ B_t(x) = spt C ∩ B_t(x) = Q_j ∩ B_t(x). Since x ∈ Q_i, (b) gives Q_i = Q_j, a contradiction. Hence Disjoint (Q_i ∩ B_ρ(z_i)) (Q_j ∩ B_ρ(z_j)) whenever Q i ≠ Q j.
2. (Every plane occurs only finitely often.) Let Q' be a subspace and I := {i : Q i = Q'}. Suppose I is infinite.
   - For every η > 0 there is i ∈ I with dist (z i) b < η. Indeed Tendsto z atTop (𝓝 b) gives N with dist (z i) b < η for all i ≥ N (Metric.tendsto_atTop), and the infinite set I has an element i > N (Set.Infinite.exists_gt).
   - (2a) b ∈ Q'. The points z i, i ∈ I, lie in Q' (z i ∈ Q i = Q'). By the previous bullet b ∈ closure Q' (Metric.mem_closure_iff). Q' is finite-dimensional, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), so b ∈ Q'.
   - (2b) Choose i ∈ I with dist (z i) b < ρ. Then b ∈ Q i (= Q') and b ∈ ball (z i) ρ, i.e. b ∈ D_i. By (G2), the hypothesis at (i, b) gives ε > 0 with HasMassDensity C y (k i) for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(b). So ε and m := k i satisfy 0 < ε ∧ ∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball b ε → HasMassDensity C y m, contradicting the instability hypothesis.
   Hence {i : Q i = Q'} is finite for every Q'.
3. (Infinitely many distinct planes.) Suppose range Q is finite. Every fibre Q ⁻¹' {Q'} is finite (step 2), so Q ⁻¹' (range Q) is finite (Set.Finite.preimage'). But Q ⁻¹' (range Q) = univ, and univ : Set ℕ is infinite (Set.infinite_univ), a contradiction. So range Q is infinite. Let e : ℕ ↪ range Q be Set.Infinite.natEmbedding (range Q) _. For each l choose i_l ∈ ℕ with Q i_l = (e l : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)). Then l ↦ Q i_l is injective, since e and Subtype.val are injective.
4. (Bounded centres.) z converges, so range z is bounded (Metric.isBounded_range_of_tendsto). Fix R with ‖z i‖ ≤ R for all i (isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le).
5. (Contradiction.) Apply the cross-branch sibling Submission.idtp_tdc_no_infinite_planar_pieces to P, C, Q* := (l ↦ Q i_l), z* := (l ↦ z i_l), ρ and R. Its hypotheses hold:
   - C is integer multiplicity and 0 < ρ.
   - finrank ℝ (Q* l) = 2, z* l ∈ Q* l and ‖z* l‖ ≤ R.
   - For l ≠ l', Q* l ≠ Q* l' (step 3), so the discs Q* l ∩ B_ρ(z* l) = D_{i_l} and D_{i_l'} are disjoint (step 1).
   - For every l and w ∈ Q* l ∩ B_ρ(z* l) = D_{i_l}, by (G3) the hypothesis at (i_l, w) gives ε > 0 with μHE[2](W ∩ Q* l) ≤ C.massOn W for every open W ⊆ B_ε(w).
   The sibling yields False. ∎
proof_key_steps: Discs on distinct planes are disjoint: subspace_eq_of_inter_ball_eq at a common point would make the planes equal.
Each plane occurs only finitely often. Otherwise b ∈ Q' (Q' is closed and z → b), b lies in one of its discs, and (G2) makes the density constant near b, contradicting the instability of b.
Finite fibres make range Q infinite. An embedding ℕ ↪ range Q gives indices i_l whose planes are pairwise distinct.
Because z converges, the centres are bounded by some R.
idtp_tdc_no_infinite_planar_pieces applied to (Q_{i_l}, z_{i_l}, ρ, R) gives False.
